--- title: "S0-03 notebook — Python" subtitle: "Build a data-check battery and grade it" jupyter: python3 execute: freeze: auto --- Eleven realistic defects have been injected into a copy of `CASE-SM`. Build the checks, then grade yourself against the manifest. ::: {#13e55541 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import pandas as pd LLOQ = 1.0 raw = pd.read_csv("../../cases/case-sm/data/ozanib_pk_messy.csv", dtype={"ID": str}) print(f"{len(raw)} rows, {raw.ID.nunique()} subjects") raw.head(4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 2643 rows, 60 subjects ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}
ID TIME NTIME DAY AMT DV EVID MDV CMT BLQ DOSE WT AGE SEX CRCL ALT DDI IPRED_TRUE
0 1 0.0 0.0 1 25.0 NaN 1 1 1 0 25 118.0 54 0 106 22 0 NaN
1 1 0.0 0.0 1 NaN NaN 0 1 2 1 25 118.0 54 0 106 22 0 0.0000
2 1 0.5 0.5 1 NaN 100.5463 0 0 2 0 25 118.0 54 0 106 22 0 120.7391
3 1 1.0 1.0 1 NaN 176.9772 0 0 2 0 25 118.0 54 0 106 22 0 165.5341
``` ::: ::: Note the `dtype={"ID": str}`. Reading identifiers as strings is a habit worth forming: pandas will happily turn `007` into `7`, and then your merge silently drops a subject. ## The battery Each check appends to a findings list rather than raising, so one run reports everything wrong at once. In production you would raise at the end if the list is non-empty — a build that continues past a failed check is not a check. ::: {#853f99dc .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} findings = [] def flag(code, msg, ids=()): findings.append(dict(code=code, message=msg, ids=sorted(set(map(str, ids))))) ``` ::: ### C01 · Identifier format ::: {#c5723b8c .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} bad = [i for i in raw.ID.unique() if str(i) != str(int(float(i)))] if bad: flag("ID_FORMAT", f"{len(bad)} ID(s) not in canonical numeric form", bad) ``` ::: ### C02 · Duplicate event keys ::: {#815f6868 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} key = ["ID", "TIME", "EVID", "CMT"] d = raw[raw.duplicated(key, keep=False)] if len(d): flag("DUP_RECORDS", f"{len(d)} rows share an (ID, TIME, EVID, CMT) key", d.ID.unique()) ``` ::: ### C03 · Negative time ::: {#e1576b46 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} d = raw[raw.TIME < 0] if len(d): flag("NEGATIVE_TIME", f"{len(d)} record(s) with TIME < 0", d.ID.unique()) ``` ::: ### C04 · Dose must sort before an observation at the same time ::: {#8436efcd .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} bad = [] for i, g in raw.groupby("ID", sort=False): for t, gt in g.groupby("TIME"): if len(gt) > 1 and gt.EVID.iloc[0] == 0 and (gt.EVID == 1).any(): bad.append(i) if bad: flag("DOSE_ORDER", "observation sorts before the dose at the same TIME", bad) ``` ::: ### C05 · Regular dosing intervals ::: {#04fd9e97 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} bad = [] for i, g in raw.groupby("ID", sort=False): dt = np.sort(g.loc[g.EVID == 1, "TIME"].values) if len(dt) == 0: bad.append(i) continue gaps = np.diff(dt) if len(gaps) and (np.abs(gaps - np.median(gaps)) > 1e-6).any(): bad.append(i) if bad: flag("MISSING_DOSE", "irregular gap in the dosing sequence", bad) ``` ::: ### C06 · Zero used to mean missing ::: {#c3d43b2b .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} d = raw[(raw.EVID == 0) & (raw.DV == 0)] if len(d): flag("ZERO_MEANS_MISSING", f"{len(d)} observation(s) with DV exactly 0", d.ID.unique()) ``` ::: ### C07 · BLQ consistency ::: {#39343fca .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} d = raw[(raw.EVID == 0) & raw.DV.notna() & (raw.DV < LLOQ) & (raw.BLQ == 0)] if len(d): flag("BLQ_IMPUTED", f"{len(d)} value(s) below LLOQ not flagged BLQ", d.ID.unique()) ``` ::: ### C08 · Unit switch Compare each subject's late concentrations against their own early ones. A within-subject comparison is far more sensitive than a population range check, because it does not have to see through between-subject variability. ::: {#73b2b592 .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} o = raw[(raw.EVID == 0) & raw.DV.notna() & (raw.TIME > 0)] bad = [] for i, g in o.groupby("ID", sort=False): early, late = g[g.TIME < 240].DV, g[g.TIME >= 240].DV if len(early) > 2 and len(late) > 0 and late.median() < early.median() / 100: bad.append(i) if bad: flag("UNIT_SWITCH", "late concentrations >100x lower than early ones", bad) ``` ::: ### C09 · Covariate plausibility ::: {#786bed70 .cell execution_count=11} ``` {.python .cell-code} d = raw[(raw.WT < 35) | (raw.WT > 250)] if len(d): flag("IMPOSSIBLE_COVARIATE", "body weight outside 35-250 kg", d.ID.unique()) ``` ::: ### C10 · Baseline covariates constant within subject ::: {#27f0c2d9 .cell execution_count=12} ``` {.python .cell-code} bad_cols = [c for c in ["AGE", "SEX", "WT", "DOSE"] if raw.groupby("ID")[c].nunique().max() > 1] if bad_cols: ids = set() for c in bad_cols: n = raw.groupby("ID")[c].nunique() ids |= set(n[n > 1].index) flag("TIME_VARYING_BASELINE", f"baseline covariate(s) vary within subject: {bad_cols}", ids) ``` ::: ### C11 · Dose magnitude ::: {#da489fb4 .cell execution_count=13} ``` {.python .cell-code} d = raw[(raw.EVID == 1) & ((raw.AMT < 1) | (raw.AMT > 1000))] if len(d): flag("DOSE_UNIT", "AMT outside a plausible 1-1000 mg range", d.ID.unique()) ``` ::: ## The report ::: {#e61eb6bc .cell execution_count=14} ``` {.python .cell-code} for f in findings: ids = ",".join(f["ids"][:6]) + ("..." if len(f["ids"]) > 6 else "") print(f"{f['code']:22s} {f['message']:55s} -> ID {ids}") print(f"\n{len(findings)} check(s) failed") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ID_FORMAT 1 ID(s) not in canonical numeric form -> ID 050 DUP_RECORDS 8 rows share an (ID, TIME, EVID, CMT) key -> ID 3 NEGATIVE_TIME 1 record(s) with TIME < 0 -> ID 27 DOSE_ORDER observation sorts before the dose at the same TIME -> ID 36 MISSING_DOSE irregular gap in the dosing sequence -> ID 8 ZERO_MEANS_MISSING 1 observation(s) with DV exactly 0 -> ID 22 BLQ_IMPUTED 43 value(s) below LLOQ not flagged BLQ -> ID 11,12,13,14,31 UNIT_SWITCH late concentrations >100x lower than early ones -> ID 11,12,13,14 IMPOSSIBLE_COVARIATE body weight outside 35-250 kg -> ID 44 TIME_VARYING_BASELINE baseline covariate(s) vary within subject: ['AGE'] -> ID 5 DOSE_UNIT AMT outside a plausible 1-1000 mg range -> ID 19 11 check(s) failed ``` ::: ::: ## Grade yourself ::: {#fae63c4c .cell execution_count=15} ``` {.python .cell-code} manifest = pd.read_csv("../../cases/case-sm/data/ozanib_pk_messy_manifest.csv") found = {f["code"] for f in findings} injected = set(manifest.code) print(f"injected : {len(injected)}") print(f"detected : {len(found & injected)}") print(f"missed : {sorted(injected - found) or 'none'}") print(f"spurious : {sorted(found - injected) or 'none'}") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` injected : 11 detected : 11 missed : none spurious : none ``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-important} Look at which subjects trip **C07** (BLQ consistency). Subjects 11–14 appear there as well as in **C08**, because dividing their concentrations by a thousand pushed them below the LLOQ. One injected defect, two independent alarms. That redundancy is the argument for running the whole battery rather than stopping at the first failure — and for reading *which* subjects each check names, not just how many checks failed. ::: ## Now fix them Detection is half the job. Each defect has a different correct response, and "correct" sometimes means *refuse to guess*. ::: {#32bc50b8 .cell execution_count=16} ``` {.python .cell-code} fixes = pd.DataFrame([ ("ID_FORMAT", "normalise in the assembly script, re-run every join"), ("DUP_RECORDS", "de-duplicate on the event key AFTER confirming they are true duplicates"), ("NEGATIVE_TIME", "decide the reference time; a screening sample may belong to a prior period"), ("DOSE_ORDER", "re-sort ID, TIME, then EVID descending"), ("MISSING_DOSE", "recover from source EX; if unrecoverable, exclude the interval and log it"), ("ZERO_MEANS_MISSING", "set to NA with MDV = 1; never carry a 0 into a log-scale model"), ("BLQ_IMPUTED", "restore the flag from the raw assay export; do not un-impute by arithmetic"), ("UNIT_SWITCH", "confirm against the laboratory report, then convert once at the boundary"), ("IMPOSSIBLE_COVARIATE", "query the site; do not silently correct a decimal point"), ("TIME_VARYING_BASELINE","take the baseline visit value; check the join key"), ("DOSE_UNIT", "confirm against source EX, then convert once"), ], columns=["code", "correct response"]) print(fixes.to_string(index=False)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` code correct response ID_FORMAT normalise in the assembly script, re-run every join DUP_RECORDS de-duplicate on the event key AFTER confirming they are true duplicates NEGATIVE_TIME decide the reference time; a screening sample may belong to a prior period DOSE_ORDER re-sort ID, TIME, then EVID descending MISSING_DOSE recover from source EX; if unrecoverable, exclude the interval and log it ZERO_MEANS_MISSING set to NA with MDV = 1; never carry a 0 into a log-scale model BLQ_IMPUTED restore the flag from the raw assay export; do not un-impute by arithmetic UNIT_SWITCH confirm against the laboratory report, then convert once at the boundary IMPOSSIBLE_COVARIATE query the site; do not silently correct a decimal point TIME_VARYING_BASELINE take the baseline visit value; check the join key DOSE_UNIT confirm against source EX, then convert once ``` ::: ::: Three of these — the missing dose, the impossible weight, the unit switch — cannot be resolved inside the analysis at all. They require going back to source. **A check that you "fix" by guessing has been converted from a defect you know about into a defect you do not.** ## What to try next 1. Add a check that every subject has at least one observation after their last dose. What does it catch that nothing above does? 2. Make C08 more general: flag any subject whose residual variability against a naive pooled fit is an order of magnitude worse than the population median. 3. Turn the battery into a function that raises on any finding, and run it as a pre-commit hook. That is the version that actually protects you.
